identity_proof.method: each process printed LOADED realpath/dev/ino/size for the file it mapped and LIB from dladdr(BN_new); the runner compared those fields with stat(2) on the expected on-disk DSO and required a /proc/self/maps entry

instrument.loader_pattern: dlopen(RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL), one libcrypto.so.3 per process, as courts/phase18/timing/bench_api.c
instrument.operation_shape: k*G as in the campaign's ctgrind harness minimal_mul.c, widened to a fixed population; k*P for the variable-base court

limitations: Internal field operations (p256::mont_reduce_into, p256::wide_mul_x86, bn::limbs::normalise) have no exported entry point and were not called directly; they are exercised only through EC_POINT_mul and ECDSA. No source-level test is substituted while claiming this court is DSO-bound.
ECDSA signatures are not compared byte-for-byte because the nonces are random; the court compares acceptance in both directions, the derived public key and the message sequence.
The candidate is the frozen distribution DSO; it was not rebuilt in this court. Its digest is checked before and after execution.
This is a compatibility/correctness court. It is not a constant-time result and not a safety conclusion.

population.derivation: scalar_for(seed, domain, i) is splitmix64 over (seed ^ domain ^ i*0x9e3779b97f4a7c15); the 32-byte big-endian result has its top bit cleared and low bit set, so it is in [1, 2^255) and therefore a non-zero P-256 scalar below n. mul-p draws j for P=j*G from domain BASE and k for k*P from domain SCALAR. ECDSA draws d from domain KEY and each message digest from domain MSG. The authority and candidate do not derive the values themselves; the harness supplies identical bytes to both.
population.description: scalar multiplications and ECDSA sign/cross-verify through the exported libcrypto.so.3 ABI
